description: Processing: Red Honey processed and sun-dried in raised beds.Varietals Grown: Arabica ( Chandragiri + S795)Altitude: 1000 mFlavour Notes: Intense floral & honey dry aroma, juicy sweet mandarin, overall a refreshing cup with good body and lingering aftertaste.  Roast: Medium Roast The estate is located in the UNESCO World heritage site of Kodagu and forms a part of the elephant corridor.Honey processed coffee is a method where coffee cherries are pulped to remove their outer skin, but the sticky, sugary layer of fruit (called mucilage) is left on the bean while it dries. Because the beans absorb the sugars from the fruit, honey processed coffees features higher sweetness with distinct notes of honey, caramel, or brown sugar. It also has a balanced profile with a creamier, heavier body than washed coffees, but less intense fruitiness than natural coffees and more mellow taste.

name: Drip Filters - Kent Microlot
description: Processing: Naturals, Patio DriedVarietals Grown: Arabica ( Kent)Altitude: 1000 m.a.s.lRoast: Medium RoastFlavour Notes:Flavour Notes: ORANGE CANDY AND BERRIES. An aromatic coffee with balanced, sparkling acidity and a fine body. It is believed that the Kent variety roots back to the first Bourbon seeds brought out of Yemen to India by Baba Budan in 1670. It originates from a selection made by Mr. L.P. Kent in 1911 from a single tree growing in his Doddengooda Estate in Mysore, South Western India. It was widely planted in India since the 1930s and became very well known for its excellent flavour profile. Slowly, due to its susceptibility to many pests and diseases, the Indian farms made a switch to hardier varieties of Arabica and Robusta. Kogilahalla Estate is one among the few estates which has managed to retain its Kent coffee plants. These old plants are specially tended to and a micro lot of ripe fruits are selectively handpicked every year. The berries are then sun dried on raised beds after a short pre-fermentation phase. With its naturally high sugar content, the pre-fermentation step lends the coffee its complex winey notes that complements the syrupy body and enhances aroma. One can easily say that Kent, hands down, is one among the most splendid Indian varieties of Arabica Coffee.
